sets.desc: Real CFA Institute Level II Mock 2, Session 1: vignettes, questions and explanations as published (44 questions, 2 h 12 min).

vignettes.body:
Lucy Wang is a derivatives trader for a South African broker-dealer. All of her firm's trades are in South African rand (ZAR) and use a 30/360 day count convention.
Wang wants to hedge a floating-rate note held by her firm against a decline in interest rates. She uses data from Exhibit 1 to price a 3 × 12 forward rate agreement (FRA).
Exhibit 1
# Maturity | Spot Market Reference Rate | Present Value Factor
3-month | 3.67% | 0.9909
6-month | 3.79% | 0.9814
12-month | 4.15% | 0.9602
Wang analyzes a receive-fixed, pay-floating interest rate swap with a fixed rate of 7.38% with a 1-year remaining maturity. The notional amount of the swap is ZAR 10,000,000 which resets semiannually. She values the swap position using the current 1-year fixed rate of 4.10% and data from Exhibit 1.
Next, Wang determines the no-arbitrage price of a bond forward contract. She uses information from Exhibit 2 and an annualized risk-free rate of 3.7%.
Exhibit 2
Quoted bond price without accrued interest (% of par) | 105.0
Future value of coupon interest (% of par) | 4.51
Accrued interest at contract initiation (% of par) | 3.00
Accrued interest at contract expiration (% of par) | 0.75
Time to forward contract expiration | 90 days
Conversion factor | 1.0
Wang then evaluates whether an arbitrage opportunity exists in 9-month forward contracts on the shares of Pintel Electronics. She is quoted a 9-month forward price of ZAR 816 by a dealer. Pintel shares currently trade at ZAR 850 and will pay a dividend of ZAR 34 in six months.

questions.q: The no-arbitrage 3 × 12 FRA fixed rate is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because this is simply the difference between the discount rates between 3 and 12 months which is: 0.9909 -0.9602 = 0.0307 = 3.07%
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because tm is ignored when annualizing the 9-month rate, as follows:
FRA0 = {[1 + LTtT]/[1 + Lhth] − 1}/tm
= {[1 + (0.0415 x 360/360)]/[1 + (0.0367 x 90/360)] − 1}
= {[1 + 0.0415]/[1 + 0.0092] − 1}
= 0.0320 = 3.20%
C. Correct.

questions.q: The value (in ZAR) of the receive-fixed interest rate swap position is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the current fixed rate of the swap is used instead of the difference, as follows:
 
VSWAP,t  = NA × (FS0 – FSt) × AP × ∑ni=1 PVi
 = 10,000,000 x 0.041 × 180 / 360 x 1.9416
 = 398,028.00
 ≈ 398,000
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the 3-month PV factors is incorrectly included when calculating the sum of the PV factors:
Spot Market Reference Rate	PV Factors
3-month	3.67%	0.9909
6-month	3.79%	0.9814
12-month	4.15%	0.9602
Σ PV	2.9325
Then the value of the swap is determined as follows:
VSWAP,t  = NA × (FS0 – FSt) × AP × ∑ni=1 PVi
= 10,000,000 × (0.0738 – 0.041) × 180 / 360 × 2.9325
= 480,930.00
≈ 481,000

questions.q: The no-arbitrage bond forward price (as a percentage of par) is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the wrong signs for AI0 (i.e. minus) and AIT (i.e. plus) are used as follows:
F0 = FV[B0 – AI0] + AIT – FVCI
= [(1 + 0.037)3/12 x (105 – 3.00)] + 0.75 – 4.51        
= [1.00912 x 102.00] – 3.76   
= 102.9307 – 3.76    
= 99.1707 
≈ 99.2
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because FVCI is incorrectly ignored as follows:
F0 = FV[B0 + AI0] – AIT – FVCI
= [(1 + 0.037)3/12 x (105 + 3.00)] – 0.75
= [1.00912 x 108.00] – 0.75   
= 108.985 – 0.75    
= 108.235 
≈ 108.4

questions.q: Does an arbitrage opportunity exist in Pintel Electronics shares?
options: Yes, by buying the shares today and selling them forward
Yes, by short selling the shares today and buying them forward
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because there is a reverse carry arbitrage opportunity available in the shares of Pintel Electronics (i.e., buy the forward and short sell the stock).
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because there is a reverse carry arbitrage opportunity available in the shares of Pintel Electronics (i.e., buy the forward and short sell the stock). Buying the shares today and selling them forward would be the correct trade if the current forward price was higher than the spot price.
C. Correct.

vignettes.body:
Charlene Norberg is an analyst for a sell-side firm. She is building valuation models for several publicly traded firms.
Norberg estimates the intrinsic value of Firm A's shares based on an FCFE model, using her forecasts in Exhibit 1. She expects long-term annual sales growth of 4% starting in Year 3, with consistent relationships between sales and net profit, changes in fixed capital, changes in working capital, and changes in debt. She estimates Firm A's cost of equity to be 9% and its WACC to be 8%.
Exhibit 1
#  | Year 1 | Year 2 | Year 3
Sales per share | $90.00 | $90.00 | $93.60
FCFE per share | $6.20 | $9.00 | $7.85
Norberg notes that, in the previous year, Firm A's FCFF was greater than its FCFE.
Next, Norberg values another firm, Firm B, which has consistently been paying dividends. The firm has a large cash balance with a growing retained earnings balance. Norberg believes that Firm B is a takeover target because it offers synergies to one of its main competitors. If a takeover does occur, Norberg expects the new owner will likely change Firm B's dividend payout and will issue debt to maintain its capital expenditures. Norberg evaluates the potential takeover from the acquirer's perspective.

questions.q: Based on Norberg's assumptions, the intrinsic value of Firm A's shares is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because n = 3 was used to compute the present value of the terminal value.
Using n = 3 incorrectly:
Item	Cash Flow	PV(Cash Flow)
Year 1 cash flow	$6.20	$5.69 = $6.20 / 1.09
Year 2 cash flow	$9.00	$7.58 = $9.00 / 1.092
Terminal value (discounted incorrectly using n = 3)	$157	$121.23 = $157 / 1.093
Sum of PV(cash flow) = $134.4960 ≈ $134.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the first constant growth cash flow (Year 3) AND the terminal value are both discounted from Year 3. In other words, the candidate double counts Year 3:
The cost of equity is 9%.
The terminal value is $7.85 / (0.09 – 0.04) = $157.
Summing the present values and double-counting the Year 3 cash flow:
$6.20/1.09 + $9.00/1.092 + $7.85/1.093 + $157/1.093
= $5.69 + $7.58 + $6.06 + $121.23 = $140.56 ≈ $141.
C. Correct.

questions.q: Which of the following would best explain the difference in Firm A's cash flow measures in the previous year?
options: Reduction in cash dividends for common stock
Repurchase of shares financed from cash balances
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the amount of cash common stock dividends does not affect either FCFF or FCFE.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because changes in cash balances or share repurchases do not affect either FCFF or FCFE.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most appropriate model to value Firm B?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the possible takeover will likely result in the new owner altering its dividend and capital structure policies.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because, with the possibility of a change in control and capital structure, the free cash flow to the firm is more appropriate as it represents funds a new owner can access to change the capital structure and payments to the firm's financing sources.
C. Correct.

questions.q: Which of the following definitions of value would be most relevant for Norberg's valuation estimate for Firm B?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because intrinsic value typically uses the present value of expected future cash flows assuming a going concern. In the case of an acquisition with alleged synergies, the stand-alone going-concern value is not the value of the target firm.
Under the efficient markets hypothesis, intrinsic value usually equals the market price of an asset. Under the rational efficient markets hypothesis, investors will not rationally incur the expenses of gathering information unless they expect to be rewarded by higher gross returns compared with the free alternative of accepting the market price. Analysts often rely on price eventually converging to intrinsic value, although intrinsic value is unobservable.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because fair market value is the price at which an asset (or liability) would change hands between a willing buyer and a willing seller when the former is not under any compulsion to buy and the latter is not under any compulsion to sell. Assuming the marketplace has confidence that the company’s management is acting in the owners’ best interests, market prices should tend, in the long run, to reflect fair market value. The transaction price, if the takeover occurs, will likely exceed Firm B's current market price due to the synergies that are believed to exist.

vignettes.body:
Fred Lang, a risk manager at an investment firm, reviews one of the firm's latest model portfolios and estimates its annual 5% parametric VaR using the information in Exhibit 1. At a 5% significance level, the critical z-value for a one-sided test is 1.65 and the critical z-value for a two-sided test is 1.96.
Exhibit 1
Monthly expected return | 1.25%
Monthly standard deviation of returns | 4.47%
Portfolio's assets under management | $200 million
Lang presents his VaR estimate to the firm's CIO. After reviewing Lang's calculation of the annual 5% parametric VaR, the CIO requests that Lang provide her with an alternative risk measure that estimates the expected loss if losses exceed the VaR cutoff.
The CIO is concerned about the underperformance of some of the firm's managed accounts relative to their benchmark. She asks Lang for his recommendation on risk constraints to help reduce her concern.
Finally, Lang prepares a presentation for an internal risk management training session. Part of this presentation focuses on the limitations of VaR.

questions.q: The annual 5% parametric VaR estimate of the model portfolio (in $ millions) is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the calculation uses the critical z-value for a two-sided test (1.96) instead of the critical z-value for a one-sided test (1.65), consequently:
VaR = {[E(Rp) − 1.96σp](−1)}(Portfolio value),
where:
E(Rp) = Annualized monthly return = (0.0125 × 12) = 0.15
σp = Annualized standard deviation = (0.0447 × 121/2) = 0.154845
Portfolio value = $200 million
VaR = −[(0.15 − 1.96 × 0.154845)] × $200 million
VaR = −[(0.15 − 0.303497)] × $200 million = $30,699,374
≈ $30.7 million
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the calculation adds rather than subtracts 1.65σp, accordingly:
VaR = [E(Rp) + 1.65σp](Portfolio value),
where:
E(Rp) = Annualized monthly return = (0.0125 × 12) = 0.15
σp = Annualized standard deviation = (0.0447 × 121/2) = 0.154845
Portfolio value = $200 million
VaR = [(0.15 + 1.65 × 0.154845)] × $200 million
VaR = [(0.15 + 0.255495)] × $200 million = $81,098,963
≈ $81.1 million

questions.q: Which of the following risk measures best addresses the CIO's request?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because conditional VaR is the average loss conditional on exceeding the VaR cutoff. Marginal VaR (MVaR) measures the change in portfolio VaR given a small change in the portfolio position. In a diversified portfolio, MVaRs can be summed to determine the contribution of each asset to the overall VaR.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because conditional VaR is the average loss conditional on exceeding the VaR cutoff. Incremental VaR measures the change in portfolio VaR as a result of adding or deleting a position from the portfolio or if a position size is changed relative to the remaining positions.

questions.q: Which of the following risk constraints would most likely reduce the CIO's concern about the managed accounts?
options: An ex ante tracking error budget
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because an ex ante tracking error budget is what mitigates the CIO's concern of deviating from (in this case, underperforming) the respective benchmark.
Some firms might use marginal VaR for each trading desk, allocating each desk a VaR budget such that the total VaR is the sum of each individual desk’s marginal VaR. A VaR budget is mainly used for risk budget allocation amongst different trading desks and does not address underperformance relative to a benchmark.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because an ex ante tracking error budget is what mitigates the CIO's concern of deviating from (in this case, underperforming) the respective benchmark.
Position limits are limits on the market value of any given investment, or the notional principal amount for a derivatives contract. Position limits mainly address concentration risks and do not address underperformance relative to a benchmark.
C. Correct.

questions.q: A limitation of the measure discussed in Lang's presentation is that it:
options: is not widely accepted by regulators.
does not facilitate capital allocation decisions.
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because regulatory reporting is an advantage of VaR, while correlation risk is a limitation. Global banking regulators also encourage banks to use VaR. These regulations require or encourage the use of VaR.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because facilitating capital allocation decisions is an advantage of VaR, while correlation risk is a limitation. The ability to compare VaR across trading units or portfolio positions provides management with a benchmark that can be used in capital allocation decisions.

vignettes.body:
Ross Wyman is a portfolio manager for a family office. He plans to add commodities to his client's holdings and meets with Tina Becker, a commodity advisor.
Wyman and Becker discuss the current market prices for three commodities, summarized in Exhibit 1.
Exhibit 1
#  | Commodity 1 | Commodity 2 | Commodity 3
Spot price | $1,688 | $830 | $87.20
Near-term futures price | $1,688 | $835 | $85.90
Farther-term futures price | $1,707 | $835 | $84.60
Becker provides additional information about Commodity 3. She notes that hedging demand by consumers currently exceeds hedging demand by producers and that the convenience yield exceeds direct storage costs.
Wyman takes a fully collateralized long futures position in Commodity 3 at a price of $84.60. Two months later, he rolls the entire position from the near-term futures contract into the farther-term futures contract. At that point, the near-term futures price is $85.50 and the farther-term futures price is $84.10. The collateral earned an annualized return of 1.2% during the two months.
Wyman also considers investing in a commodity index. His objective is to select the index that provides the largest contribution to performance based on the following two expectations:
trending commodity markets, where outperforming assets continue to go up in price and underperforming assets continue to drift lower;
no changes in the shapes of forward curves, with some markets currently in backwardation and others in contango.

questions.q: Based on current market prices, which commodity has a negative calendar spread?
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the calendar spread is zero. It is defined as the difference between the near-term futures contract price and the farther-term futures contract price, namely $835 – $835 = $0.
This is the only commodity where the futures price exceeds the spot price. However, the difference between spot price and futures price (here, $830 – $835 = –$5) is called basis and not calendar spread.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the calendar spread is positive. It is defined as the difference between the near-term futures contract price and the farther-term futures contract price, namely $85.90 – $84.60 = $1.30. 
This commodity would have a negative spread if the definition of the calendar spread was incorrectly reversed ($84.60 – $85.90 = –$1.30).

questions.q: Based on Exhibit 1 and Becker's additional information, the shape of the futures price curve of Commodity 3 is most consistent with the:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the insurance theory explains the situation of backwardation with the fact that there is more hedging by producers than consumers. Alternatively, this theory posits that the futures price has to be lower than the current spot price as a form of payment or remuneration to the speculator who takes on the price risk and provides price insurance to the commodity seller. However, the case states that hedging by consumers exceeds hedging by producers, which is inconsistent with the insurance theory, given that the market is in backwardation.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the hedging pressure hypothesis describes the shape of the price curve with reference to relative hedging demand. The case states that there is more demand for hedging from consumers than from producers. Based on the hedging pressure hypothesis, this will lead to a situation of contango. However, Commodity 3 is in backwardation.

questions.q: The 2-month total return of Wyman's position in Commodity 3 is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the roll return is calculated incorrectly by reversing near-term and farther-term futures prices in the numerator. The total return is the sum of price return, roll return, and collateral return as follows:
Price return = (Current price – Previous price)/Previous price = ($85.50 – $84.60)/$84.60 = 0.01063830
Roll return for the entire position is calculated incorrectly by reversing near-term and farther-term futures prices as follows: (Farther-term futures price – Near-term futures price)/Near-term futures price = ($84.10 – $85.50)/$85.50 = –0.01637427
Collateral return for 2 months (based on a fully collateralized position and an annualized return of 1.2%) = 0.012 × 2/12 = 0.002
Total return = 0.01063830 – 0.01637427 + 0.002 = –0.00373597 ≈ –0.4%
If the denominator is also incorrectly swapped when calculating the roll return, we get: (Farther-term futures price – Near-term futures price)/Farther-term futures price = ($84.10 – $85.50)/$84.10 = –0.01664685. In this case, the total return is incorrectly calculated as 0.01063830 – 0.01664685 + 0.002 = –0.00400855 ≈ –0.4%.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the collateral return is calculated for one year and not for two months. The total return is the sum of price return, roll return, and collateral return as follows:
Price return = (Current price – Previous price)/Previous price = ($85.50 – $84.60)/$84.60 = 0.01063830
Roll return for the entire position = (Near-term futures price – Farther-term futures price)/Near-term futures price = ($85.50 – $84.10)/$85.50 = 0.01637427
Collateral return (based on a fully collateralized position) is incorrectly taken for 1 year: 0.012
Total return = 0.01063830 + 0.01637427 + 0.012 = 0.03901257 ≈ 3.9%

questions.q: Based on his objective regarding the commodity index investment, Wyman should select an index that:
options: rebalances frequently and contains a large percentage of constituents in backwardation.
rebalances frequently and contains a small percentage of constituents in backwardation.
rebalances infrequently and contains a large percentage of constituents in backwardation.
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because frequent rebalancing can lead to underperformance in a trending market, because the outperforming assets are sold, but will continue up in price, whereas the underperforming assets are purchased, but will drift lower. With regard to backwardation, commodity sectors in backwardation typically improve index returns. This is because backwardation leads to positive roll returns.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because frequent rebalancing can lead to underperformance in a trending market, because the outperforming assets are sold, but will continue up in price, whereas the underperforming assets are purchased, but will drift lower. Also, a small percentage of constituents in backwardation limits the potential for positive roll return. Instead, a large percentage of constituents in backwardation is preferred.  
C. Correct. Correct because in markets that are trending, infrequent rebalancing coupled with a large percentage of constituents in backwardation provides the largest contribution to performance among the three options. With regard to rebalancing, frequent rebalancing can lead to underperformance in a trending market, because the outperforming assets are sold, but will continue up in price, whereas the underperforming assets are purchased, but will drift lower. With regard to backwardation, commodity sectors in backwardation typically improve index returns. This is because backwardation leads to positive roll returns. So a large percentage of constituents in backwardation is preferred.

vignettes.body:
Amanda Mond, a junior analyst, is valuing two consumer cyclical companies: Delong and Gruseb.
Delong
Delong is a growing company in a cyclical industry with volatile earnings. Mond summarizes Delong's book value per share (BVPS) and ROE for the most recent year in Exhibit 1. She compares these metrics to their respective averages over the most recent business cycle and over the long term. She then normalizes Delong's EPS using the average ROE method.
Exhibit 1
# | Most Recent Year | Average Over Most Recent Business Cycle | Long-Term Historical Average
BVPS | EUR 11.2 | EUR 10.5 | EUR 9.6
ROE | 15.0% | 16.0% | 17.5%
Mond next uses the following forecasted fundamentals to calculate Delong's justified trailing P/E.
Dividend payout ratio of 46%
ROE of 15%
Required rate of return of 10.8%
Mond wants to calculate an industry benchmark multiple for Delong based on the multiples of its competitors. She observes that the range of competitor multiples is bounded by zero on the downside but includes very large outliers. Mond uses a measure of central tendency that mitigates the impact of these very large outliers, but not the small outliers.
Gruseb
Gruseb is a manufacturer of small household appliances. Mond observes that there are significant differences in both the duration of growth and the expected earnings growth between Gruseb and its peers. She considers using the PEG ratio as an alternative valuation method to the P/E ratio to address these differences.

questions.q: Based on the average ROE method, Delong's normalized EPS is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because it multiplies the average book value per share over the business cycle by the average ROE over the business cycle instead of using the book value per share for the most recent year:
Normalized EPS = 16.0% × EUR 10.5 =1.68
The same answer can be obtained by multiplying book value per share by ROE for most recent year as well as the average over 5 years.
Normalized EPS = EUR 11.2 ×15% = 1.68
Normalized EPS = EUR 9.6 ×17.5% = 1.68
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because it multiplies the long-term historical average ROE by the book value per share for the most recent year instead of using the average ROE over most recent business cycle:
Normalized EPS = 17.5% × EUR 11.2 = 1.96

questions.q: Based on Mond's forecasted fundamentals, Delong's justified trailing P/E is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the calculation uses the dividend payout ratio rather than the retention rate, giving a value of 14.8.
Formula for justified trailing P/E: 
P0/E0 = (1 – b)(1 + g)/(r – g)
Using the wrong b = 0.46.
Given the ROE of 15%, g = b × ROE = 0.46 × 15% = 6.9%.
Required rate of return, r = 10.8%
Justified trailing P/E = (1 – 0.46) × (1 + 0.069)/(0.108 – 0.069) = 14.802 or 14.8
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because this is the calculation of justified forward P/E rather than justified trailing P/E, giving a value of 17.0.
Formula for justified forward P/E:
P0/E1 = (1 – b)/(r – g)
Delong's dividend payout ratio is 46%, thus making b = (1 – 0.46) = 0.54.
Given the ROE of 15%, g = b × ROE = 0.54 × 15% = 8.1%.
Required rate of return, r = 10.8%
Justified forward P/E = (1 – 0.54)/(0.108 – 0.081) = 17.037 or 17.0
C. Correct.

questions.q: Which of the following measures of central tendency should Mond use to calculate the industry benchmark multiple?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the median mitigates the impact of both large and small outliers. Using the median rather than the arithmetic mean to derive an average multiple mitigates the effect of outliers. This would also mitigate an impact of small outliers, but such outliers are already bounded by zero on the downside.
The harmonic mean is more appropriate as the competitor's multiples are bounded by zero on the downside, but include very large outliers, and Mond wants to use a measure of central tendency, which mitigates the impact of large, but not small outliers.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the arithmetic average is impacted by outliers, especially the large outliers. Mond wants to use a measure of central tendency, which mitigates the impact of large outliers, and therefore the harmonic mean would be more appropriate.

questions.q: Will the alternative valuation method that Mond considers address the two growth differences between Gruseb and its peers?
options: No, it will not address the difference in the duration of growth
No, it will not address the difference in expected earnings growth
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because although PEG ratio addresses the impact of earnings growth, it does not account for the difference in growth duration.
A metric that appears to address the impact of earnings growth on P/E is the P/E-to-growth (PEG) ratio. The PEG ratio is calculated as the stock’s P/E divided by the expected earnings growth rate (in percentage terms).
The PEG ratio does not account for differences in the duration of growth. For example, dividing P/Es by short-term (five-year) growth forecasts may not capture differences in long-term growth prospects.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because PEG ratio addresses the impact of earnings growth.
A metric that appears to address the impact of earnings growth on P/E is the P/E-to-growth (PEG) ratio. The PEG ratio is calculated as the stock’s P/E divided by the expected earnings growth rate (in percentage terms).

vignettes.body:
Dora Kriser, a financial analyst, is currently evaluating the intercompany investments and earnings quality of Delphine Industries, a large diversified consumer products company that reports under IFRS.
Delphine recently announced that it would be increasing its ownership interest in Company A from 35% to 50%. Delphine and Company A are both profitable. Kriser considers how Delphine's net profit margin might be affected after the increase in ownership under the following scenarios:
Scenario 1: Delphine exercises significant influence, but not control, over Company A.
Scenario 2: Delphine exercises control over Company A.
Kriser is concerned that recent industry changes may negatively affect one of Delphine's cash-generating units. She evaluates the following projections to determine the expected impairment loss under IFRS:
Carrying value of cash-generating unit: €18,200,000
Recoverable amount of cash-generating unit: €17,700,000
Goodwill allocated to cash-generating unit: €300,000
Next, Kriser analyzes Delphine's earnings quality. She begins by examining the cash component and accrual component of Delphine's recurring earnings. Based on this examination, she expects Delphine to continue to exhibit a high degree of earnings persistence.
Finally, Kriser examines Delphine's statement of cash flows and observes that interest paid is classified as an operating activity and interest received is classified as an investing activity. She considers whether these cash flow classifications could affect comparisons with competitors that report under US GAAP.

questions.q: Delphine's net profit margin under Scenario 1 would be:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because sales would be higher under Scenario 2, while net income would be the same under Scenario 1 and Scenario 2, making net profit margin (net income / sales) higher under Scenario 1. This answer incorrectly assumes that sales is the same under both scenarios but that net income is higher under consolidation (Scenario 2), or that net income is the same under both scenarios but that sales is lower under Scenario 2.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because sales would be higher under Scenario 2, while net income would be the same under Scenario 1 and Scenario 2, making net profit margin (net income / sales) higher under Scenario 1. This answer incorrectly assumes that the equity method (Scenario 1) and consolidation (Scenario 2) have the same effect on net income and sales.
C. Correct.

questions.q: Based on Kriser's projections, the expected impairment loss for Delphine's cash-generating unit is:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the impairment loss under IFRS is the difference between the recoverable amount and the carrying value of the cash-generating unit. This answer choice assumes that the impairment loss is the difference between the excess carrying value and the recorded goodwill of the cash-generating unit.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the impairment loss (the difference between these two amounts) is first applied to the goodwill that has been allocated to the cash-generating unit. Once this has been reduced to zero, the remaining amount of the loss is then allocated to all of the other non-cash assets in the unit on a pro rata basis. This answer choice assumes that the impairment loss is limited to the goodwill allocated to the reporting unit.
C. Correct.

questions.q: Which of the following best supports Kriser's expectation for Delphine's earnings persistence?
options: The cash component of Delphine's earnings is less than the accrual component
The cash component of Delphine's earnings is equal to the accrual component
The cash component of Delphine's earnings is greater than the accrual component
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because a lower cash component of earnings is consistent with less (not more) persistent earnings.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because a higher (not equal) cash component of earnings is consistent with more persistent earnings.
C. Correct.

questions.q: Is Delphine's classification of interest paid and interest received consistent with competitors that report under US GAAP?
options: No, the classification of interest paid is not consistent
No, the classification of interest received is not consistent
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because IFRS also permits companies to classify interest and dividends received as operating or as investing. In contrast, US GAAP requires that interest paid, interest received, and dividends received all be classified as operating cash flows. Thus, Delphine's classification of interest received as investing is not consistent with competitors that report under US GAAP.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because IFRS permits companies to classify interest paid either as operating or as financing. In contrast, US GAAP requires that interest paid, interest received, and dividends received all be classified as operating cash flows. Thus, Delphine's classification of interest paid as operating is consistent with competitors that report under US GAAP.
C. Correct.

vignettes.body:
Marcia Garrett is a research analyst at IGMA Investments. IGMA is a large investment firm that claims compliance with the Standards.
While preparing a report on industry trends, Garrett read an article that appeared in a leading business newspaper. Included in the article was a summary of a study conducted by a prominent trade association. Garrett did not obtain a copy of the study directly from the trade association, but did however include information from the article in her report. Garrett cites only the newspaper in her report.
During the most recent quarter, Garrett prepared an analysis detailing her interest rate expectations over the next year and submitted it to IGMA's investment committee. Her research is to be included as part of a wider report by the firm regarding market expectations for the year ahead. Based on her analysis, Garrett's opinion is that interest rates will remain fairly stable. The committee disagrees with some of Garrett's assumptions and does not include her opinion in the wider report. The committee's final report issues a consensus expectation that interest rates will increase and includes detailed assumptions supporting that view. Despite the difference in opinions, Garrett acknowledges that the committee's conclusion has a reasonable basis. The final report is distributed to clients and includes Garrett's name, as well as other research analysts who contributed to the report as authors.
Garrett is part of a working group asked to review IGMA's code of ethics and to suggest any necessary changes that are needed to ensure that it is consistent with the Standards. During one of the working group's discussions, Garrett states that the Standards recommend that the code of ethics include general fiduciary concepts as well as detailed compliance procedures.
Garrett has accepted an offer to join a rival firm. While at IGMA, Garrett and a colleague developed a quantitative model that was used for industry and company analysis. Garrett considers if she can continue to use the model at her new firm.

questions.q: Did Garrett violate the Standards in her report on industry trends?
options: Yes, because she did not cite the trade association
Yes, because she did not independently review the trade association report
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because in all instances, a member or candidate must cite the actual source of the information. Best practice would be either to obtain the complete study from its original author and cite only that author or to use the information provided by the intermediary and cite both sources. An unprepared candidate might select this response believing that the media outlet citation is sufficient.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because there is no requirement that the analyst independently review third-party research. From the reading, in the case of distributing third-party, outsourced research, members and candidates may use and distribute such reports as long as they do not represent themselves as the report’s authors. Indeed, the member or candidate may add value for the client by sifting through research and repackaging it for clients. Therefore, there is no violation of Standard I(C) - Diligence and Reasonable Basis. An unprepared candidate might select this option believing that such reports must be independently reviewed.

questions.q: Were the Standards violated in the publication of the investment committee report?
options: Yes, because Garrett's opinion should have been included
Yes, because Garrett should not have been listed as an author
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the conclusions or recommendations of the group report represent the consensus of the group and are not necessarily the views of the member or candidate, even though the name of the member or candidate is included on the report. An unprepared candidate might select this response believing that group research reports must reflect the opinions of all the authors.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because if the member or candidate believes that the consensus opinion has a reasonable and adequate basis and is independent and objective, the member or candidate need not decline to be identified with the report. If the member or candidate is confident in the process, the member or candidate does not need to dissociate from the report even if it does not reflect his or her opinion. An unprepared candidate might select this response believing that dissenting analysts must dissociate from the group report.

questions.q: Is Garrett's statement about the Standard's recommendation for the code of ethics correct?
options: No, with regard to compliance procedures
No, with regard to general fiduciary concepts
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard IV(C) states stand-alone codes of ethics should be written in plain language and should address general fiduciary concepts. They should be unencumbered by numerous detailed procedures. Further, separating the code of ethics from compliance procedures will also reduce, if not eliminate, the legal terminology and boilerplate language that can make the underlying ethical principles incomprehensible to the average person. An unprepared candidate might select this response believing that a code of ethics that is compliant with the Standards should include detailed compliance procedures.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard IV(C) states stand-alone codes of ethics should be written in plain language and should address general fiduciary concepts. They should be unencumbered by numerous detailed procedures. An unprepared candidate might select this response believing that a code of ethics that is compliant with the Standards should not include general fiduciary concepts.

questions.q: Would Garrett violate the Standards if she uses the quantitative model at her new firm?
options: Yes, unless she receives permission from IGMA
Yes, unless she receives written permission from her colleague at IGMA
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because when members and candidates are planning to leave their current employer, they must continue to act in the employer’s best interest. Activities that might constitute a violation, especially in combination, include self-dealing (appropriating for one’s own property a business opportunity or information belonging to one’s employer). The quantitative model developed with her colleague at AGM is the property of AGM. Thus, Garrett must receive permission from AGM to use the model at the new firm. An unprepared candidate might select this response believing that, because Garrett developed the model with another colleague, she is free to use it at the new firm.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because when members and candidates are planning to leave their current employer, they must continue to act in the employer’s best interest. Activities that might constitute a violation, especially in combination, include self-dealing (appropriating for one’s own property a business opportunity or information belonging to one’s employer). The quantitative model developed with her colleague at AGM is the property of AGM. Thus, Garrett must receive permission from AGM to use the model at the new firm. An unprepared candidate might select this response believing that, because Garrett developed the model with another colleague, she must receive permission from her colleague to use it at the new firm.

vignettes.body:
Marietjie Granger works for a South African equity fund manager specializing in ETFs. She is evaluating several potential ETF investments and the use of factor models in investment decision-making.
Granger evaluates ETF Zulu and notices that its share price is currently trading at a higher than the usual premium to the NAV of its underlying equities. She considers how the authorized participants may take advantage of this pricing differential.
Granger wants to make a 6-month tactical investment in ETF X-Ray. She determines the expected holding period cost using the following information:
Bid-ask spread: 0.15%
One-way commission: 0.10%
Annual management fee: 0.20%
Granger also analyzes a portfolio of smart beta ETFs using the Carhart model. She calculates the equilibrium expected return on the portfolio using the factor sensitivities and returns in Exhibit 1. The risk free rate is 4.5%.
Exhibit 1
# | Factor Sensitivity | Factor Return
Market risk (RMRF) | 1.0 | 2.5%
Capitalization (SMB) | –1.8 | –1.7%
Book-to-market (HML) | 0.7 | 2.1%
Momentum (WML) | 0.2 | 2.8%
Finally, Granger evaluates the multifactor models used by two European equity ETFs to construct their portfolios. One of the ETFs uses a statistical factor model, while the other uses a macroeconomic factor model. She makes the following conclusions regarding the two models:
Conclusion 1: An advantage of statistical factor models is that they make minimal assumptions.
Conclusion 2: The interpretation of macroeconomic factors is more difficult than statistical factors.

questions.q: To take advantage of the pricing differential in ETF Zulu, the authorized participants could:
options: buy back ETF Zulu shares from investors.
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect. The unprepared candidate may think that redeeming ETF Zulu shares (selling the underlying securities and buying ETF Zulu shares) is the expected reaction from the APs. This would be the case if the ETF was trading at a discount to its NAV.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect. The unprepared candidate who does not understand the redemption/creation process may think that APs will buy back ETF Zulu shares from investors to keep the ETF in a tighter range around the NAV.

questions.q: The expected holding period cost for Granger's investment in ETF X-Ray is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect. The candidate gets to this option by not adjusting the management fee for the six-month investment period as follows:
= (One-way commission % × 2) + (1/2 × Bid–ask spread % × 2) + Management fee for period (%)
= (0.10% × 2) + (1/2 × 0.15% × 2) + (0.20%)
= 0.20% + 0.15% + 0.20%
= 0.55%
C. Incorrect. Incorrect. The candidate gets to this option by multiplying the full bid-ask spread by two as follows:
= (One-way commission % × 2) + (Bid–ask spread % × 2) + Management fee for period (%)
= (0.10% × 2) + (0.15% × 2) + (6/12 × 0.20%)
= 0.20% + 0.30% + 0.10%
= 0.60%

questions.q: Based on the Carhart model, the equilibrium expected return on the portfolio of smart beta ETFs is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect. The candidate gets to this option by omitting the risk-free rate (i.e., calculates excess return) as follows:
E(Rp) = RF + βp,1RMRF + βp,2SMB + βp,3HML + βp,4WML
= (1.0 ´ 2.5) + (‒1.8 ´ ‒1.7) + (0.7 ´ 2.1) + (0.2 ´ 2.8)
= 2.5 + 3.06 + 1.47 + 0.56
= 7.59
B. Incorrect. Incorrect. The candidate gets to this option by adding the factor returns to the risk-free rate, i.e. he/she does not multiply them with the betas:
E(Rp) = RF + βp,1RMRF + βp,2SMB + βp,3HML + βp,4WML
= 4.5 + 2.5 ‒ 1.7 + 2.1 + 2.8
= 10.20
C. Correct.

questions.q: Are both of Granger's conclusions regarding the multifactor models used by the European equity ETFs correct?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect as Conclusion 1 is correct, but Conclusion 2 is incorrect. The unprepared candidate may choose this option if he/she correctly reasons that (1) Conclusion 1 is correct, and incorrectly reasons that (2) because statistical factor models make minimal assumptions, statistical factors are also easier to interpret than macroeconomic factors.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect as the interpretation of macroeconomic factors is easier than statistical factors. The unprepared candidate may choose this option if he/she incorrectly reasons that (1) Conclusion 1 does not seem plausible because it seems that statistical models could make more assumptions, and incorrectly reasons that (2) macroeconomic factors are more difficult to interpret than statistical factors.

vignettes.body:
Jennifer Francis is a currency specialist helping clients manage their foreign exchange exposures. All currencies are quoted as the amount of the numerator currency per one unit of the denominator currency (e.g., USD/EUR is quoted as the amount of USD per 1 EUR).
Francis is working with a client looking to execute a trade in the Thai baht (THB) and Australian dollar (AUD) currency pair. Francis receives a bid–offer quote in THB/AUD (24.3065/24.3090) from a dealer and compares this to the interbank market quotes in THB/USD (33.3942/33.3965) and USD/AUD (0.7276/0.7279) to see if an arbitrage opportunity exists.
Stephan Podowski is a client of Francis' located in Country A, whose currency is the FXA. Podowski's company will receive a payment in Country B's currency (FXB) in 18 months, and he is considering using a forward contract to hedge the currency exposure. Francis uses the following information to determine the forward discount for a 540-day FXA/FXB forward contract:
FXA/FXB spot exchange rate: 1.1423;
540-day market reference rate (annualized, Actual/360) for Country A: 1.23%;
540-day market reference rate (annualized, Actual/360) for Country B: 5.52%.
Nine months ago, Podowski bought EUR 20 million forward against the USD by entering into a 1-year forward contract at 1.1308 USD/EUR. He wants to calculate the mark-to-market value of this position today. The current USD/EUR spot rate is quoted at 1.1352/1.1355 and the 90-day forward points are –14/–12. The annualized 90-day market reference rate (Actual/360) is 0.53% for USD and 0.77% for EUR.
Francis is looking for potential carry trades to recommend to her clients. She focuses on a potential trade between the AUD and the South African rand (ZAR). She reviews what market conditions are required for the trade to be profitable.

questions.q: Based on the dealer's quote, does an arbitrage opportunity exist in the THB/AUD currency pair?
options: Yes, by selling AUD to the dealer and buying AUD in the interbank market
Yes, by buying AUD from the dealer and selling AUD in the interbank market
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the AUD is offered in the interbank market at 24.3093 THB/AUD while the dealer's bid is 24.3065 THB/AUD, so the trade would incur a loss of 24.3093 – 24.3065 = 0.0028. The cross-rate implied by the interbank market does not provide an arbitrage opportunity.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the AUD is offered from the dealer at 24.3090 THB/AUD while the interbank market bid is 24.2976 THB/AUD, so the trade would incur a loss of 24.3090 – 24.2976 = 0.0114. The cross-rate implied by the interbank market does not provide an arbitrage opportunity.

questions.q: The forward points for the FXA/FXB forward contract are closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the price currency's interest rate is used in the denominator instead of the base currency's. This gets: 
1.1423 × [(540/360) / (1 + 0.0123(540/360))] × (0.0123 – 0.0552)
= –0.072175 ≈ –0.0722, 
which when turned into forward points = (–0.0722 × 10,000)
= –722 forward points.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the formula used is for one year instead of 18 months (540 days). This gets: 
1.1423 × [(360/360) / (1 + 0.0552(360/360))] × (0.0123 – 0.0552)
= –0.046441 ≈ –0.0464, 
which when turned into forward points = (–0.0464 × 10,000)
= –464 forward points.

questions.q: The mark-to-market value of Podowski's USD/EUR forward contract is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the offer, and not the bid, is used for the offsetting contract. The all-in offer rate is 1.1355 – 12/10,000 = 1.1343 USD/EUR.
EUR 20 million × 1.1343 USD/EUR = USD 22,686,000. This gives a positive cash flow of USD 70,000 (22,686,000 – 22,616,000). Discounted at the 90-day MRR, the PV equals:
USD 70,000 / [1 + 0.0053(90/360)] = USD 69,907.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the forward points are subtracted, which gives an all-in bid rate of 1.1352 – (–14/10,000) = 1.1366 USD/EUR. 
On settlement, Podowski will pay USD 22,616,000 (20,000,000 × 1.1308) on the original forward and receive USD 22,732,000 (20,000,000 × 1.1366) from the offsetting forward, resulting in a positive cash flow of USD 116,000 (22,732,000 – 22,616,000). Discounted at the 90-day MRR, the PV equals:
USD 116,000 / [1 + 0.0053(90/360)] = USD 115,847.

questions.q: What condition would best support Francis' trade proposal between AUD and ZAR?
options: Covered interest rate parity not holding in the short term
The interest rate differential between the two countries being expected to widen after the trade is initiated
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because for a carry trade to succeed, it is uncovered interest rate parity, not covered interest rate parity, that must not hold. If it held, the investor would receive identical returns from either an unhedged foreign currency return or a domestic currency investment as the appreciation or depreciation of the exchange rate would offset the yield differential. If uncovered interest rate parity held at all times, investors would not be able to profit from a strategy that undertook long positions in high-yield currencies and short positions in low-yield currencies. The change in spot rates over the tenor of the forward contracts would cancel out the interest rate differentials locked in at the inception of the position.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the difference in yields is locked in at the time of the trade, so the movement of the yield spread once the trade is initiated is irrelevant.

vignettes.body:
Liying Wang manages her firm's investment-grade bond portfolio. She considers purchasing a senior unsecured bond issued by AHM Manufacturing (the AHM01 bond) for the portfolio. This bond is rated BBB, has a 2-year maturity, and has a 5% annual coupon. Wang assumes a recovery rate of 40% and uses a government yield binomial interest rate model to estimate the fair value of the AHM01 bond. Selected information for the bond is presented in Exhibit 1. Given no default, the value of the AHM01 bond is 100.46.
Based on her assumptions and the information in Exhibit 1, Wang purchases the AHM01 bond at a price equal to its fair value.
Exhibit 1
# Year | Expected Exposure | Probability of Default | Discount Factor
1 | 105.49 | 2.25% | 0.9524
2 | 105.00 | 2.20% | 0.9115
Wang’s junior analyst estimates that the recovery rate for the AHM01 bond will be 30%. Holding all else equal, Wang considers how this estimate would affect her valuation of the bond.
Wang purchases protection on the AHM01 bond using a single-name CDS. The counterparty for the transaction is XRM Bank. The CDS has a standard annual coupon of 100 basis points and the current market spread on AHM01 bonds is 150 basis points. The initial value of the CDS contract is set to zero.
Finally, Wang makes the following observations regarding two other investment-grade bonds, Bond X and Bond Y, each of which has a 5-year maturity and is option-free:
Bond X trades at a credit risk premium of 2.50% over the reference rate; the risk premium implied by the CDS market is 2.25%.
Bond Y trades at a credit risk premium of 2.50% over the reference rate; the risk premium implied by the CDS market is 2.75%.
Believing that the disparity in risk premiums is temporary, Wang considers a basis trade.

questions.q: The price of the AHM01 bond is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because it computes the LGD as Expected Exposure times the Recovery Rate.
Year 1:  LGD = 40% × 105.49 = 42.196
Year 2:  LGD = 40% × 105.00 = 42.000
CVA per year is then equal to POD times LGD times the discount factor:
Year 1:  CVA = 0.0225 × 42.196 × 0.9524 = 0.9042
Year 2:  CVA = 0.0220 × 42.000 × 0.9115 = 0.8422
CVA = sum of the yearly CVA = 1.7464
Value of Bond = VND – CVA = 100.46 – 1.7464 = 98.7136 ≈ 98.71
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because it computes the bond value as VND – Year 1 CVA: 
100.46 – 1.3563 = 99.1037 ≈ 99.10

questions.q: Based on the recovery rate estimated by the junior analyst, the probability of default of the AHM01 bond would be:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the probability of default would need to be reduced from its current value of 2.25%.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the probability of default would be lower than 2.25%.

questions.q: The CDS protection that Wang purchases on the AHM01 bond requires:
options: Wang to make an upfront payment.
XRM Bank to make an upfront payment.
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because an upfront payment is required in this case to set the value of the CDS equal to zero on the trade date. As stated in the case, the initial value is set to zero. Since the CDS has a standardized fixed coupon of 100 basis points while the risk premium fair price of CDS protection is 150 basis points, a payment must be made by Wang to set the value equal to zero.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because an upfront payment is made by Wang to XRM Bank. As stated in the case, the initial value is set to zero. Since the CDS has a standardized fixed coupon of 100 basis points while the risk premium fair price of CDS protection is 150 basis points, a payment must be made by Wang to set the value equal to zero.

questions.q: For the basis trade, Wang should:
options: buy Bond X and sell protection.
buy Bond X and buy protection.
buy Bond Y and buy protection.
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the correct basis trade is to buy Bond X and to buy protection since compared to the bond market, the CDS market is pricing in credit risk that is low compared to the bond market.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the correct basis trade involving Bond Y is to sell Bond Y and to sell protection. Bond Y currently looks overpriced compared to the CDS market (its credit spread is 2.50%; the CDS risk premium is 2.75%) and one can buy the credit risk of Bond Y by selling protection. Investing the proceeds of the sale of Bond Y in a risk-free bond, combined with the sale of protection, essentially replicates a cheaper way to purchase Bond Y.

vignettes.body:
Maya Keegan, CFA, is a private wealth manager at Stanz Investments, which has adopted the Standards as part of its ethics and compliance policy. Stanz does not claim compliance with the GIPS standards.
Keegan is invited to join the leadership team of her local CFA society as treasurer. Her responsibilities will include monitoring the asset allocation of the society's reserve funds. Keegan will receive annual compensation for the position as treasurer. Separately, she is asked to join the board of Kino Empire, a small publicly traded movie theater chain founded by a family friend. Many of Keegan's client accounts invest in Kino Empire's shares. Keegan has opted to receive no monetary compensation if she accepts this board position, although she will receive free movie tickets for her personal use at all Kino Empire theaters.
At a local CFA society event, Keegan meets a CFA candidate who just took the Level II exam. During the conversation with Keegan, the candidate comments that her employer expects her to complete the CFA Program even though she is convinced that it is not relevant for her current position as a trader. To support her claim, the candidate cites a question on the recent Level II exam that tested how different accounting methods affect company balance sheets.
In the performance presentation section of her firm's marketing materials, Keegan provides details of an investment model recently developed by a Stanz analyst. She first notes that the model's performance is based on results from a simulated backtest. She then shows a comparison of this simulated performance with the actual past performance of a weighted composite of similar accounts she currently manages. Keegan ensures that all closed accounts are excluded when determining the performance of this composite.
Keegan supervises an assistant wealth manager who has a good track record of managing client accounts. However, the assistant wealth manager has accumulated significant personal credit card debt due to his poor personal spending habits. He also regularly participates in legal poker games with friends. He would like to set up a plan to reduce his debt and is seeking personal financial advice from Keegan.

questions.q: According to the Standards, does Keegan need to obtain written permission from Stanz before accepting the CFA society and the Kino Empire positions?
options: No, only for the CFA society position
No, only for the Kino Empire position
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because Keegan must obtain written permission to accept both the CFA society position and the Kino Empire position.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because Keegan must obtain written permission to accept both the CFA society position and the Kino Empire position.

questions.q: During the conversation with Keegan at the local CFA society event, does the CFA candidate violate the Standards?
options: Yes, because of her comment about the recent Level II exam
Yes, because of her comment about the relevance of the CFA Program
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because, according to Standard VII(A) Conduct as Participants in CFA Institute Programs, examples of information that cannot be disclosed by candidates sitting for an exam include but are not limited to specific details of questions appearing on the exam. Therefore, the CFA candidate violates the Standards by detailing the specific exam question about how alternative accounting methods affect company balance sheets.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because Standard VII(A) does not cover expressing opinions regarding CFA Institute, the CFA Program, or other CFA Institute programs. As a result, the CFA candidate's comment about the relevance of the CFA Program is not a violation of the Standards.

questions.q: Regarding the performance presentation section of the marketing materials, are Keegan's actions consistent with the Standards?
options: No, because of the treatment of closed accounts
No, because of the use of simulated results from the backtest
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because Keegan excludes any closed accounts when determining the performance of the composite and is therefore not consistent with the Standards.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because, according to the recommended procedures for Standard III(D) Performance Presentation, members and candidates can also meet their obligations under Standard III(D) by including disclosures that fully explain the performance results being reported (for example, stating, when appropriate, that results are simulated when model results are used). In the case, Keegan provides details of the model and shows a comparison with actual performance history. Therefore, her actions with respect to the simulated backtest are consistent with the Standards.

questions.q: With regard to his personal situation, does the assistant wealth manager violate the Standard relating to misconduct?
options: Yes, because of his spending habits
Yes, because of his activity with friends
questions.why:
A. Correct. 
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because, while the assistant wealth manager has accumulated significant personal debt, it is not a result of acts that reflect adversely on his professional reputation, integrity, or competence.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the assistant wealth manager's participation in legal poker games with friends does not involve any illegal activity or affect his professional responsibilities.

vignettes.body:
Bella Stone is an analyst covering Garnet Corp. To forecast the price of Garnet shares, she starts by examining related economic data and estimates a log-linear trend in the economic variable most relevant to her analysis. Stone evaluates whether the log-linear trend model suffers from serially correlated errors. The Durbin–Watson test statistic from the regression is 0.54 and the lower critical value for the Durbin–Watson statistic is dl = 1.25.
Stone predicts Garnet's EPS using quarterly data in a first-order autoregressive model, AR(1). She tests for and rejects the presence of a unit root. The model estimation is presented in Exhibit 1. In the most recent quarter, EPS was $0.96. The critical t-statistic is 2.04.
Exhibit 1
# Regression Statistics | 
R2 | 0.2059
Standard error | 0.0856
Observations | 32
Durbin–Watson statistic | 1.56

Intercept | 0.4485 | 0.1457 | 3.08
EPSt–1 | 0.4541 | 0.1572 | 2.89

Autocorrelations of the Residual

1 | –0.0572 | 0.1768 | –0.32
2 | 0.0705 | 0.1768 | 0.40

Stone also incorporates machine learning into her modelling. She gathers transaction-level data for a set of Garnet bonds and provides an excerpt of the dataset in Exhibit 2. Stone prepares to wrangle the extracted raw data.
Exhibit 2

Stone evaluates if the model can properly classify the "Type" feature into "buy" or "sell," and examines the model training performance for validation of the model. She compiles the confusion matrix in Exhibit 3.

questions.q: Based on the Durbin–Watson test, the errors in the economic variable's trend model are:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the Durbin–Watson statistic has a value of 0.54, which is lower than the lower critical value of dl = 1.246. Therefore, we can reject the null hypothesis that correlation is <= 0 and conclude that correlation > 0.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the Durbin–Watson statistic has a value of 0.54, which is lower than the lower critical value of dl = 1.246. Therefore, we can reject the null hypothesis that correlation is <= 0 and conclude that correlation > 0.
C. Correct.

questions.q: The 1-period-ahead forecast of Garnet's EPS is:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the mean-reverting level is incorrectly calculated as:
xt = b0/b1
where b0 and b1 are the parameter estimates from an AR(1) model specified as
xt+1 = b0 + b1xt
Taking the parameter estimates from the exhibit:
b0 = 0.4485
b1 = 0.4541
The incorrect mean-reverting level xt = 0.4485/0.4541 = 0.9877
The current value of 0.96 < the incorrect mean-reverting level of 0.9877.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the mean-reverting level is incorrectly assumed to be the most recent value of 0.96, in which case the current value of 0.96 = the incorrect mean-reverting level of 0.96.
C. Correct.

questions.q: Which variable in the excerpt of the machine-learning dataset has a non-uniformity error?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because, although the price data in the exhibit do not have the same values for each observation, they are all presented in the same format. 
Non-uniformity error is where the data are not present in an identical format.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because type has an inaccuracy error, not a non-uniformity error. One of the observations is marked "trade" and is not labeled as a "buy" or a "sell."
Non-uniformity error is where the data are not present in an identical format.
Inaccuracy error is where the data are not a measure of true value. This can be rectified with the help of business records and administrators.
C. Correct.

questions.q: The confusion matrix indicates that model accuracy is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because this is model precision, not accuracy. Precision is the ratio of correctly predicted positive classes to all predicted positive classes.
Precision (P) = TP/(TP + FP)
For classification problems, error analysis involves computing four basic evaluation metrics: true positive (TP), false positive (FP), true negative (TN), and false negative (FN) metrics. FP is also called a Type I error, and FN is also called a Type II error.
From the case:
TP = 70
FP = 40
Precision = 70/(70 + 40) = 70/110 = 0.6364 ≈ 0.64
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because this is model recall, not accuracy. Recall (also known as sensitivity) is the ratio of correctly predicted positive classes to all actual positive classes.
Recall (R) = TP/(TP + FN)
For classification problems, error analysis involves computing four basic evaluation metrics: true positive (TP), false positive (FP), true negative (TN), and false negative (FN) metrics. FP is also called a Type I error, and FN is also called a Type II error.
From the case:
TP = 70
FN = 20
Recall = 70/(70 + 20) = 70/90 = 0.7778 ≈ 0.78

vignettes.body:
Minah Lee, CFA, recently joined Caldecott Asset Management as a portfolio manager. Lee resides in a country where the securities laws and regulations are stricter than the Code and Standards. Caldecott is based in a neighboring country with securities laws and regulations that are less strict than the Code and Standards. All of Caldecott's clients are based in the firm's home country. In both countries, applicable law states that the law of the locality where business is conducted governs.
Caldecott hires a consultant to establish an ESG screening process for stock selection. Lee prepares an investment memo recommending the new screening process to Caldecott's clients. It includes a description that states "we will include the consultant's proprietary ESG factors when filtering out unsuitable stocks." The memo also discusses significant risks of the process, including that "the ESG screening process is subjective and may contradict conclusions from other ESG selection processes." The memo ends by stating that "this process will reduce the risk of portfolios suffering from unanticipated climate risk and will guarantee superior returns."
Lee receives automated sell recommendations from Caldecott's portfolio allocation software to ensure all client portfolios match the recommendations from the ESG screen. After securing approval from selected clients with IPS that are suitable to adopt the new ESG screen, Lee begins executing sell trades in these client accounts. Lee decides not to keep records for the sell trades since Caldecott's software has automated the ESG screen recommendations. Lee then reinvests the cash generated by the sell trades to maintain the same level of equity market exposure. She manually selects stocks to buy for the accounts and prepares notes justifying these buy trades. Lee retains trade records for five years as part of the firm's regulatory compliance.
Lee joins the board of trustees at the local university. The position is unpaid but is likely to be time consuming in the first year. She also starts a position as an adjunct professor at the university. The compensation from the university includes government-mandated defined contributions to a retirement plan. Lee decides to allocate the retirement plan assets to a large diversified mutual fund managed by Caldecott's competitor. Lee obtained written approval from Caldecott for her compensation as an adjunct professor but did not disclose her board position and how the retirement plan assets are invested.

questions.q: In the event of a conflict of rules or regulations at work, Lee must adhere to the:
options: securities laws and regulations of Caldecott's country.
securities laws and regulations of Lee's home country.
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the applicable law in Caldecott's country is less strict than the Code and Standards. Based on Standard I(A) Knowledge of the Law, Lee must therefore adhere to the Code and Standards.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the applicable law states that the law of the locality where the business is conducted governs. Based on Standard I(A) Knowledge of the Law, since business is conducted in Caldecott's country, Lee must adhere to the Code and Standards, which are stricter than the laws of Caldecott's country. 
This choice might be correct if Lee were conducting business with another resident of her home country. However, Caldecott's clients are based in Caldecott's country.

questions.q: In the memo regarding the ESG screening process, does Lee violate the Standard relating to communication with clients and prospective clients?
options: Yes, because Lee fails to appropriately separate fact from opinion
Yes, because Lee fails to sufficiently communicate the risks associated with the screening process
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the memo fails to appropriately distinguish opinion from fact. Standard V(B) Communications with Clients and Prospective Clients requires that opinion be separated from fact.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the memo communicates significant risks including the key risk that the recommendations are subjective and may be contradicted by other ESG screens. According to Standard V(B) Communications with Clients and Prospective Clients, members and candidates must outline to clients and prospective clients significant risks and limitations of the analysis contained in their investment products or recommendations. The memo discusses significant risks of the new process and is therefore compliant with Standard V(B).

questions.q: Lee violates the Standard relating to record retention with respect to the:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because Standard V(C) Record Retention only requires Lee to maintain appropriate records to support her investment actions. Lee prepares notes justifying the buy trades executed in the client accounts. Her notes are likely sufficient to explain the decisions to increase each stock's weight in the client accounts.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because this is a CFA Institute recommendation only in the absence of regulatory guidance or firm policies. It is not a must do for Lee to impose this requirement on her employer. 
As per the guidance to Standard V(C) Record Retention, in the absence of regulatory guidance or firm policies, CFA Institute recommends maintaining records for at least seven years.

questions.q: With respect to the university, does Lee violate the Standard relating to disclosure of conflicts?
options: Yes, by failing to disclose the retirement plan investment
Yes, by failing to disclose her position on the board of trustees
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because Standard VI(A) Disclosure of Conflicts requires Lee to disclose to her employer her involvement with the university's board of trustees. Lee's new role as a trustee can reasonably be expected to be time consuming, to the possible detriment of Lee's responsibilities at Caldecott, at least in the first year.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the application of Standard VI(A) Disclosure of Conflicts would not require Lee to disclose her personal or retirement investments in large diversified mutual funds, unless specifically required by her employer.
C. Correct.

Jessica Gunning is an analyst reviewing US-based GameDay Inc.'s cost of capital and corporate restructuring actions.
For GameDay's cost of capital, Gunning begins by determining GameDay's cost of equity and uses a macroeconomic model to estimate the equity risk premium (ERP). She forecasts the data shown in Exhibit 1 and applies the Grinold-Kroner model.
Exhibit 1

Growth rate in P/E ratio | 0.0%

Next, Gunning estimates GameDay's current cost of debt. GameDay has a single outstanding bond issue – a straight unsecured bond with a remaining maturity of four-years. The issue is thinly traded and there is no reliable market-based YTM available. Gunning uses matrix pricing to estimate the bond's yield. She notes that the average YTM on similarly rated bonds at more liquid two- and five-year maturities are 5.57% and 6.14%, respectively.
To improve sales in a new product segment, GameDay recently acquired StopGap Inc. for $33.80 per share. Gunning assesses whether the acquisition was fairly priced using the comparable transactions method and the information in Exhibit 2. When calculating a weighted average estimated price, she assigns a weight of 50% to the price-to-sales (P/S) multiple, and a 25% weight to each of the other two multiples. She considers the acquisition to be fairly priced if the price paid is within $1 of her estimate on a per share basis.

P/S ratio | 2.1
StopGap Inc. Information
EPS | $2.20

Sales per share | $17.90
Several months pass and GameDay announces that a rival firm has offered $1.6 billion to acquire its Southern product segment. Southern has produced EBITDA of $140 million in the most recent year and Gunning estimates that a spinoff of Southern would achieve an EV/EBITDA multiple of 14. She evaluates which is the better choice: accept the divestment offer or begin the spinoff process of the segment.

Stephen Russo is a treasury analyst at Central Finance Inc., which specializes in financing equipment and real estate. Russo and his manager, Ericka Patry, meet to discuss anticipated changes to interest rates and the potential impact on Central Finance's portfolio.
Patry and Russo discuss the differences between Treasury rates and swap rates for the same maturity. Russo makes the following two comments.

Comment 2: Given the opportunity for arbitrage, differences between the two rates are minimal

Patry and Russo next discuss the term structure of interest rates. Russo accepts the theory that yields are solely a function of the supply and demand for funds at a particular maturity.
Central Finance manages yield curve risk using key rate durations and reviews portfolio exposures when there is a 25 basis point change in the yield curve. The Treasury rate can differ from the swap rate for the same term for several reasons. Unlike the cash flows from US Treasury bonds, the cash flows from swaps are subject to greater default risk. Market liquidity for specific maturities may differ. For example, some parts of the term structure of interest rates may be more actively traded with swaps than with Treasury bonds.

Joao Viniciu is an equity analyst researching Pedra S.A., a Brazilian multinational corporation. Pedra reports under IFRS with a fiscal year end of 31 December. Its reporting currency is the Brazilian Real (BRL).
Viniciu analyzes the sustainability of net sales growth for each of Pedra’s geographic segments. Exhibit 1 shows the components of total net sales growth for each of these segments.
Exhibit 1
# Geographic Segment | Contribution from Volume Growth | Contribution from Price Growth | Contribution from Foreign Currency Exchange | Total Net Sales Growth
Europe | 4.6% | 1.9% | 1.4% | 7.9%
Americas | 0.7% | 1.1% | 4.3% | 6.1%
Asia Pacific | 3.6% | 2.1% | 1.8% | 7.5%
For his research, Viniciu uses the BRL/USD (number of BRL per 1 USD) exchange rate information for the most recent year as shown in Exhibit 2.
Exhibit 2
BRL/USD
1 January | 5.07
1 November | 5.53
31 December | 5.45
Average for the year | 5.26
On 1 November of the most recent year, Pedra purchased imported goods worth USD 3.2 million on credit from an unaffiliated US supplier. The amount payable for these imported goods by Pedra was still outstanding as of 31 December.
Carro Corp. is one of Pedra’s wholly-owned US-based subsidiaries. Pedra translates Carro’s financial statements using the current rate method based on the rates in Exhibit 2. Carro's only non-monetary assets are inventory and fixed assets, while all of its liabilities are monetary. Carro's inventory and fixed assets were purchased at a BRL/USD rate of 5.24. Viniciu analyzes the effect of the translation method on Carro’s debt-to-assets ratio for the most recent year.
Over the current year, Viniciu expects that Carro will maintain a stable net asset balance sheet exposure and that the BRL will weaken against the USD.

questions.q: Based on the components of total net sales growth, which of Pedra's geographic segments has the lowest sustainable growth rate?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because although Europe’s net sales growth has the highest contribution from volume growth (4.6%), it has a relatively small contribution from the less sustainable changes in the foreign currency exchange rate (1.4%). Europe has a combined contribution from the volume and price components (4.6% + 1.9% = 6.5%) which are the most sustainable components.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because Asia Pacific’s net sales growth has the highest contribution from price change (2.1%), it has a relatively small contribution from the less sustainable changes in the foreign currency exchange rate (1.8%). Asia Pacific has a combined contribution from the volume and price components (3.6% + 2.1% = 5.7%) which are the most sustainable components.

questions.q: For the most recent year, Pedra's purchase of imported goods resulted in a foreign exchange:

A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the calculation uses the right exchange rates but reverses the direction of the rates.

questions.q: After translation, Carro’s debt-to-assets ratio at 31 December of the most recent year was:
options: lower than it was before translation.
the same as it was before translation.
higher than it was before translation.
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the debt-to-assets ratio will be the same before (computed with the USD financial statements) and after translation (computed with the BRL financial statements). 
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the debt-to-assets ratio will be the same before (computed with the USD financial statements) and after translation (computed with the BRL financial statements). If Pedra had applied the temporal method, non-monetary assets and liabilities would be translated using the historical exchange rate. As the exchange rate used to translate non-monetary assets was lower at time of purchase (BRL/USD 5.24) than at reporting date (BRL/USD 5.45), total assets would have been lower and debt-to-total assets would have been higher.

questions.q: Based on Viniciu’s expectations, the translation of Carro’s financial statements in the current year will most likely result in a:
options: translation loss in Pedra's income statement.
translation gain in Pedra's income statement.
positive translation adjustment in Pedra's shareholders’ equity.

A. Incorrect. Incorrect because Carro’s financial statements in the current year will most likely result in a positive translation adjustment in stockholders’ equity. Carro is expected to maintain a stable net asset balance sheet exposure, and the BRL will weaken against the USD (i.e., the foreign currency will strengthen against the presentation currency). Therefore, the translation of Carro’s financial statements in the current year will most likely result in a positive translation adjustment which will be reflected in stockholders’ equity because Pedra uses the current rate method to translate Carro's financial statements. If Carro used the temporal method for translation and there was a strengthening of the BRL, there would have been a translation loss recognized in the income statement.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because Carro’s financial statements in the current year will most likely result in a positive translation adjustment in stockholders’ equity. Carro is expected to maintain a stable net asset balance sheet exposure, and the BRL will weaken against the USD (i.e., the foreign currency will strengthen against the presentation currency). Therefore, the translation of Carro’s financial statements in the current year will most likely result in a positive translation adjustment which will be reflected in stockholders’ equity because Pedra uses the current rate method to translate Carro's financial statements. If Carro used the temporal method for translation then there would have been a translation gain recognized in the income statement.
